## A — the first rebase, onto af54c70c39
The ref-mutating commands, in the order run, from inside the nested checkout:
$ git switch -c fusion/stas-390-tool-channel-authority refs/heads/fusion/stas-389-tool-channel-authority
  Previous HEAD position was af54c70c39 RUFU-307: refuse agent-authored text carrying code points outside the operator allowlist

$ git rebase refs/heads/main            (main was then af54c70c39)

Tip produced: b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7
No conflict occurred, so 'git rebase --abort' was never needed and neither side of
any hunk was edited. The card body's prediction held for the reason it measured:
trunk had not touched either of this line's two paths since the merge-base — the
'trunk delta since merge-base' probe in raw/ac1-subsumption.txt is an empty
name-only list, and merge-tree between trunk and the pre-rebase tip was rc=0.

### AC2 landing predicate measured against the base it was built on (af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9)
Everything in this section is computed from the pinned SHA, not from
refs/heads/main, because refs/heads/main moved later in this run (section B).
Recomputing section A against a live ref would rewrite history in this file.
$ git rev-list --left-right --count af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9...b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7
  0	2      (left = trunk-only = 0; right = commits the branch carries)
$ git rev-list --count b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7..af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9
  0                    (0 = nothing on trunk was missing from it)
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9 b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7   -> rc=0   (0 = that trunk WAS contained)
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7 af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9   -> rc=1   (1 = it was NOT inside trunk)
Both directions printed, because a single rc is directionally ambiguous.
$ git diff --shortstat af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9...b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7
   2 files changed, 275 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
three-dot form on purpose: the two-dot form would report trunk's own commits as
this branch's contribution.

## B — the base moved during this card's run (the hazard this card exists for)
At Step 4, after the rebase and after the red-green capture had been written, the
same read of the same ref that Steps 0 and 2 read returned a different SHA:
$ git rev-parse refs/heads/main
  read #1 and #2 : af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9     (start of Step 0; start of Step 2)
  read #3        : 06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396     (start of Step 4)
$ git log --format='%h %aI %s' af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9..06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396
  06b1768b18 2026-11-05T13:54:35+01:00 RUFU-441: evict memory snapshots the consolidation sweep produces
$ git rev-list --left-right --count 06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396...b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7
  1	2      (left = 1: the delivered-after-A branch was now BEHIND trunk)
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396 b1884a46d2f59605e45a6f6d85ad7806bbcfd5f7   -> rc=1   (1 = no longer fast-forwardable)
So the AC2 predicate '0 N' that section A legitimately satisfied stopped being
true roughly as this step was being written. The AC1 rule to read the trunk twice
is what makes that visible instead of silent: the recorded SHA is checked against
the live ref again before any landing instruction is written, and it disagreed.

### Why the drift cannot have touched what this card verified
The moving commit is a memory-snapshot eviction change. Over the two paths this
line owns, the two trunk tips are the same bytes:
$ git rev-parse af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9:packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts 06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396:packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts
  3f942b3db329f34811d60147e854a49b58e74b61
  3f942b3db329f34811d60147e854a49b58e74b61
$ git rev-parse af54c70c391e8318e80994c2c4cd10c8f53544f9:packages/pi-claude-cli/src/__tests__ 06b1768b18f38a9b4d0d5b35467204e25bfe4396:packages/pi-claude-cli/src/__tests__
  57aec8708db4710cd99261f3cd1a99d8c03e9b47
  57aec8708db4710cd99261f3cd1a99d8c03e9b47
Same blob for the module, same tree object for the whole tests directory. The
red-green capture in raw/red-green.txt therefore tests the same pre-fix code under
either base, and no suite result had to be re-earned for that reason alone.

## The mechanical proof that this card authored no code — TWO measurements

### (1) diff scoped to the card's own two paths, pre-rebase tip to delivered tip
$ git diff --stat 22f6d6c5b1 d38b478184 -- packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts packages/pi-claude-cli/src/__tests__/
  (empty output — zero files, zero lines)
Empty means the two paths this line owns are byte-identical from the pre-rebase
tip all the way through BOTH rebases. It is scoped deliberately. The UNscoped
old-tip to new-tip diff is non-empty BY CONSTRUCTION whenever trunk moved,
because it then also carries the trunk delta since merge-base. Measured here so
nobody has to guess which number means what:
$ git diff --shortstat 22f6d6c5b1 d38b478184   (UNscoped — expected non-empty, NOT a code change)
   60 files changed, 4081 insertions(+), 139 deletions(-)
Those files are the trunk commits the line caught up with — 7 of them,
one more than the rebase itself performed, because of the drift in section B.
Neither the executor nor a later reviewer may read that unscoped number as a
silent code change: measurement (1) plus measurement (2) is the proof, and it is
satisfied.
The same scoped check between the two rebases' own tips, which is the narrower
question 'did rebase C change anything rebase A had not already':
$ git diff --stat b1884a46d2 d38b478184 -- packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts packages/pi-claude-cli/src/__tests__/
  (empty output — zero files, zero lines)

### (2) full range-diff — every carried commit must map to '='
$ git range-diff 3c8ece6606f16ab13174be0e78b2c50e18e62dd8 22f6d6c5b1 d38b478184
   -:  ---------- >  1:  8584c966f9 RUFU-448: write the park-clear history line before the clear and isolate per-card failures
   -:  ---------- >  2:  8f1ecb6e72 fix(RUFU-883): stop the 5s metrics read from shipping comment text it never reads
   -:  ---------- >  3:  6aff48faff test(RUFU-883): teach the pg parity matrix the `comments` member it could not know about
   -:  ---------- >  4:  0d31daba2c test(RUFU-307): make the fn_task_done summary fixture charset-legal so the guard cannot refuse it
   -:  ---------- >  5:  bff234b429 RUFU-456: expose the post-merge evidence contract in the workflow editor and Settings
   -:  ---------- >  6:  af54c70c39 RUFU-307: refuse agent-authored text carrying code points outside the operator allowlist
   -:  ---------- >  7:  06b1768b18 RUFU-441: evict memory snapshots the consolidation sweep produces
   1:  203afd2c9f =  8:  3bd7bc9c14 STAS-389: stop a tool result from writing its own frame or a role key
   2:  22f6d6c5b1 =  9:  d38b478184 STAS-389: prove frame and role authority are gone, per surface, red then green
verdict column extracted: [==]
Parse shape: sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//' then awk '/^[0-9]+:/ { printf "%s", $3 }'.
range-diff right-aligns its two commit counters, so a carried line may begin with
padding — an earlier version of this parser anchored on '^[0-9]:' and silently
returned nothing once the right-hand counter reached two digits. After stripping
the padding, field 3 is the character sitting between the old and the new commit,
so only a carried commit can contribute one; the '-:' lines have no old-side
commit and contribute nothing. Both characters are '=' — no '!' (content changed)
and no missing or extra entry in the carried range.
The lines reading '-:  ---------- > N:' are the trunk commits that exist only on
the right, which is what rebasing onto a moved tip looks like; they are not
content differences. (This git build has no 'range-diff --format'.)
The first rebase's own range-diff, for completeness, over the base it used:
$ git range-diff 3c8ece6606f16ab13174be0e78b2c50e18e62dd8 22f6d6c5b1 b1884a46d2   -> verdict column [==]

  identical: YES at the moment of this capture
$ git rev-parse refs/heads/fusion/stas-389-tool-channel-authority   (predecessor, must be unmoved)
  22f6d6c5b11338f32e15bec81f1338a6c367c757   (identical to the pre-rebase tip 22f6d6c5b11338f32e15bec81f1338a6c367c757)
$ git rev-parse refs/heads/fusion/stas-388-tool-result-authority    (predecessor, never checked out)
  6a59cf4d51feaa0293869d4343d6395c3f37d6ff
Every mutation this card made was 'git switch -c' (a new branch) or 'git rebase'
onto a ref it only read. refs/heads/main advanced because something else landed
into it; this card never wrote it.

## Drift probe for the operator — run this immediately before landing
Trunk moved once inside this card's own run, so a landing instruction written now
is a statement about a moving target. These two commands are the whole check:
$ git rev-list --left-right --count refs/heads/main...refs/heads/fusion/stas-390-tool-channel-authority
  expect 0 2. Anything but 0 in the left column means trunk moved again since this
  capture; re-run 'git rebase refs/heads/main' on that branch and re-run the
  sentinel suite before merging. Nothing about the card's judgement changes, only
  the tip, which is exactly the property a content-free rebase is supposed to have.
$ git diff --stat 22f6d6c5b1 refs/heads/fusion/stas-390-tool-channel-authority -- packages/pi-claude-cli/src/tool-result-authority.ts packages/pi-claude-cli/src/__tests__/
  expect EMPTY, before and after any further rebase. A non-empty answer is the
  sentinel that code got authored, and it must stop the landing.
